findings.evidence: "Put flags before the `resume` subcommand." There is no stated failure mode. The verified fact in docs/audit/recovery/codex/facts.md that `resume` rejects `-s` and `-C` with `unexpected argument` is not in the skill.

findings.evidence: "pass a model only when the user names one or the task needs a specific one... Ask only when an unresolved choice affects the result." "The task needs a specific one" and "unresolved choice" are vague for a step that is otherwise exact.
findings.fix: Make the default explicit: use the configured default model and the effort from the mapping, and ask only when the user's request conflicts with the configured default or names an effort the model does not support.

findings.evidence: The 7 evals cover read-only, edit, resume, flags, the Git gate and a failed version check. None covers the cross-project `--last` fallback to a session id, or a network need that should use the narrow workspace-write network setting before `danger-full-access`. Several trigger queries are short with no file paths or context (for example "Create an architecture diagram of the Codex CLI integration.").
findings.fix: Add two evals (resume from another project using a session id, and a network-required task that checks the narrow setting is tried first). Replace the easy negatives with near-misses that carry context, such as a path and a request to explain a codex exec error without running it.

findings.evidence: "add `--approve-for-me` (it routes approval requests through automatic review inside the workspace-write sandbox)". This is a version-sensitive CLI flag with no source URL or check date in the skill. Preflight 2 reads --help only when support is uncertain, and the flag's source and date are in facts.md only. Facts not verified online.
findings.fix: Add the source and date next to the flag, for example "(`codex exec --help`, codex-cli 0.162.1; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cli/reference, checked 2026-11-07)". Or require running `codex exec --help` to confirm the flag exists before using it.

findings.evidence: "NEVER add a global override (a `git config --global` change, a user-level settings edit) the user did not ask for" is generic and rarely met by a command-file writer. The strongest gotchas (bang-line state change, unquoted shell splice, blind retry, silent shadowing, dropped frontmatter) carry the specific, non-obvious reasons.
findings.fix: Tie the global-override item to a concrete command-writing case, such as a generated body that runs `git config --global`, or fold it into the existing authorization gotcha.

findings.evidence: "...tell users to quote a multi-word value; when a value may contain spaces and you cannot rely on quoting, take `$ARGUMENTS` whole... confirm the indexing there before relying on `$0` versus `$1`" leaves the agent to decide in a fragile area.
findings.fix: State one default: use `arguments:` only for single-token values and `$ARGUMENTS` whole for anything that may hold spaces. Keep the doc link as the escape hatch.

findings.evidence: The 18 queries (10 should-trigger, 8 should-not-trigger) include no should-trigger query for updating an existing command, although the description says "Create or update" and evals.json has an approved-update case.
findings.fix: Add one should-trigger query such as "my /deploy-preview command should run the tests first, can you change it?" and one near-miss negative (for example, a request to explain what an existing command does).

findings.evidence: "`make fix` (runs `uv run ruff check --fix --unsafe-fixes`)" and "`ruff format --check`" are vendor CLI flags stated with no source URL or check date, and no instruction to read them live.
findings.fix: Add the source and date after the table (https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/linter/ and https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/formatter/, checked <date>), or say to confirm with `ruff check --help`.

findings.evidence: Step 2: "say a skill fits better (out of scope here) and stop without writing. If the user still wants a command, write one..." The stop and the continue branch are not sequenced. The agent has to guess whether to wait for the user's answer first.
findings.fix: Reword it as: say a skill fits better, ask whether to proceed with a command that calls the scripts by path, and write nothing until the user answers.

findings.evidence: When a fact is unknown (cause, date, owner), say it is unknown and do not promise a future update... The decision rule for unknown facts is in Audience and accuracy checks.
findings.fix: This restates line 39 outside the Gotchas list. Fold it into one NEVER-style gotcha with the reason: an invented promise gets repeated upstream as a commitment. Do not remove the content; merge it and record the merge.

findings.evidence: Description is a long list of artifact types and exclusions (about 900 characters), close to the 1024 limit.
findings.fix: Draft and improve software-team emails, Slack/Teams messages, stakeholder status updates, escalations, review and help requests, meeting agendas (standup, planning, retro, 1:1, design or code review), meeting summaries and team communication norms. Use when translating technical work for non-technical audiences without inventing metrics, making an async request actionable, or choosing a channel across time zones, even if the user only says 'make this clearer' or 'tell the execs'. Not for difficult feedback (feedback-mastery), sales copy, legal documents, sentence-level style edits (writing-clearly-and-concisely) or scheduling meetings.
